JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed under Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the death caused in a Road Traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioners in the nutshell is that on 09.12.2023 at about 6.28 p.m, the deceased was proceeding as pedestrian, returning by walk towards her home from her land along with her father-in-law, on the left side of Balepura - Channarayapatna Road, near Narayanappa Land by observing all the traffic rules and regulations,
at that time a driver of Tipper Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-43-A-1551 proceeding on the same direction with high speed in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger the human life and dashed against the deceased.
Due to the terrific impact the deceased fell down on the road, the Tipper lorry ran over the deceased and thereby she sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident she was Manjunatha Also Called As C.N. ... vs Narayanaswamy N on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82891407/
2 shifted to Akash Hospital, Devanahalli, wherein the duty doctors declared as dead.

sentences.text: It is submitted that postmortem was conducted at Government Hospital, Devanahalli and corpse was handed over to the family members.
It is further submitted that because of death of deceased the petitioners have suffered both financially and emotionally.
The accident was caused due to the sole negligence of driver of Tipper Lorry.
The respondents No.1 and 2 being the owner and insurer thereof are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
3. Notice was duly served to respondent No.1.
Respondent No.1 appeared through his counsel by filing written statement rather objections to the main petition contending that the petition itself is not maintainable either law or on facts.

This respondent has denied that the involvement of the vehicle, date and place of accident and also denied the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Tipper lorry.
The respondent No.2 admitted that he is the RC owner of the Tipper Lorry and was duly insured with the 2 nd respondent and same was in force as on the date of accident.
Further it is contended that the petitioners by colluding with the police have falsely implicated the vehicle in order to wangle the compensation from this respondent.
There is no nexus to the respondent and alleged accident and the said vehicle is not responsible for the accident.
It is further urged that in case if court comes to conclusion that the petitioner is entitle for any compensation same is to be fastened on the 2nd Respondent - insurance company.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.
4. After service of notice, respondent No.2 appeared and filed written statement contending that the petition itself is not maintainable either law or on facts.
This respondent admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of Goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-43-A-1551.
However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms & conditions of the policy.
Non -compliance of section's 134(c), 158(6) of MV Act is pleaded.
Further negligence on the part of the driver of its insured vehicle is denied.
Per contra it is alleged that the unfortunate accident occurred on account of the sole negligence of the deceased without having a proper lookout at the vehicular movement on the road.

Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the driver of the insured vehicle did not possess valid & effective DL and further the said insured vehicle did not holding valid and effective Permit and FC.
Despite knowing the said fact the owner thereof had handed over its possession to such a driver.
On account of willful breach of the terms & conditions of the policy by the insured, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him.
Rest of the petition averments are contended as false and baseless and it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners proves that they are the legal heirs and dependents of the deceased ?
2) Whether the petitioners prove that the deceased succumbed to the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident that occurred on 09.12.2023 at about 6.28 to 6.40 p.m., near Narayanappa Land on Balepura - Channarayapattana, Channarayapattana Manjunatha Also Called As C.N. ... vs Narayanaswamy N on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82891407/
3
Hobli, Bengaluru District, due to actionable negligence of the driver of Tipper Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-43-A-1551 ?

3) Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation as prayed? If so, at what rate and from whom ?
4) What order or award ?
6. Petitioner No.1 examined himself as PW.1.
Ex's.P1 to 28 were marked on behalf of the petitioners.
Further the petitioners have also examined the Investigating Office as PW.2.
The respondents did not choose to lead any evidence on its behalf.
7. Heard arguments of both sides.
Perused the entire materials placed on record and arguments.

My answers to the above issues are as follows :-
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.4 : As per final order for the  following :
 REASONS 8. ISSUE NO.2 : As this issue clinches the whole dispute in controversy, this issue is taken for discussion at the inception for better appreciation of evidence and dissection of materials placed on record.
The petitioners have knocked the doors of justice with a relief to grant a compensation on account of death of deceased in a Road Traffic Accident.
Before discussing the disputed facts in issue it is relevant to have look into the case of petitioners in a nutshell.

9. It is the case of petitioners that on 09.12.2023 at about 6.28 p.m, the deceased was proceeding as pedestrian, returning by walk towards her home from her land along with her father-in-law, on the left side of Balepura - Channarayapatna Road, near Narayanappa Land by observing all the traffic rules and regulations, at that time a driver of Tipper Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-43-A-1551 proceeding on the same direction with high speed in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger the human life and dashed against the deceased.
Due to the terrific impact the deceased fell down on the road, the Tipper lorry ran over the deceased and thereby she sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident she was shifted to Akash Hospital, Devanahalli, wherein the duty doctors declared as dead.

It is further urged that the accident happened because of rash and negligent driving of the driver of Tipper lorry and as such the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
Hence prayed to allow the petition.

On the other hand, the respondents denied the involvement of the vehicle in the accident and same is falsely implicated to have caused the accident.
Further it is contended that the deceased was knockdown by the unknown vehicle.
It is specifically urged that the insured vehicle is planted in this case.
It is further urged that the petitioners have played fraud in falsely implicating the insured vehicle so as to wangle the more compensation which is not tenable in the eye of law.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.
In support of these contentions, the respondents have not examined any witnesses in this regard.
12. The petitioners in order to prove the factum of involvement of Tipper Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-43-A-1551 has mainly relied on Ex.P.1 to 13 being police documents.

The learned counsel for respondents contending that in Ex.P.2 complaint the registration number of the offending vehicle is conspicuously missing, as such the insured vehicle is implicated at the time of filing charge sheet so as to deceive respondent and wangle more compensation amount.
When this being specific and positive contention urged by the respondents, let me analyze the materials placed on record in the light of settled principles of law.
It could be borne out from the Ex.P.2 complaint itself that the accident had happened on 6.40 p.m on 09.12.2023.
Ex.P.2 complaint was filed on very same day at 2.00 A.M. (morning).
To put in encapsulated form, soon after the lapse of just 8 hours from the time of the accident the criminal law was set into motion.
Ex . P2
is filed by the husband of of deceased.
No doubt in the said complaint the registration of the offending vehicle is not mentioned.
But in the said complaint it is clearly narrated the manner of accident.
Based on Ex.P.2 complaint, the Ex.P.1 FIR was lodged.
It is relevant to note that Ex.P.13 charge sheet was filed as against the Tipper Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-43-A-1551.

It could be borne out from the evidence of PW.2 who is the Investigating officer that he has narrated that on the basis of the statement given by the eye witness and such other circumstantial evidence the driver of Tipper Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-43-A-1551 was taken into custody.
Much was canvassed with regard to the cross examination of PW.2.
At this juncture it is relevant to note that there is absolutely no delay in lodging complaint.
The Ex.P.2 complaint was lodged by husband of the deceaed.
When such is the case while analyzing the case filed under benevolent legislation this Court cannot expect strict proof of the same.
No strict proof of evidence can be expected in claim petition of like nature.
PW.2 during his cross examination had deposed that previous IO has filed FIR, Inquest Mahazar and thereafter further investigation he was done.
He admitted that in FIR the vehicle number is not mentioned, but the the offending vehicle colour is stated to be white colour.
He stated that he appointed the staff for assertain the vehicle.
He came to know that one while colour tipper lorry has always been traveled in the said road, which belongs to owner of one Swamy Weigh bridge by name Narayanaswamy.
He called him and enquired, on enquiry he confirmed that said lorry caused accident.
Then he issued notice u/s 133 of M.V.Act to the owner.
On 16.12.2023 the owner of the vehicle replied to the notice.
He admitted that eye witness have not disclosed the registration number of the lorry.
From his evidence it could be culled out there is absolutely no toxic nexus between the respondent No.1 who being the owner of the offending vehicle and the petitioners.
Further it is also not the case of respondent No.2 that there is an active collusion of respondent No.1 with that of petitioners herein.

Further it is also not the case of the respondent No.2 that the accused in Crime No.139/2023 of Manjunatha Also Called As C.N. ... vs Narayanaswamy N on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82891407/

But the evidence of Investigating Officer goes to show that the offending vehicle was involved in the accident.

In order to prove the contention urged in the petition with regard to the involvement of the vehicle it is relevant to relied on the decision reported in 2011 ACJ 1261 in case of Oriental Insurance Company Limited v/s Reena Awathi and others Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Alahabad held that,
"When motorcycle number was not disclosed in FIR but it was detected during investigation.

On the same point of law it is relevant to relied on the decision reported in 2012 ACJ 2569 in case of Shalini and others V/s Harbhajan and others, wherein it was held "merely non mentioning number of the vehicle in the FIR its not sufficient until and unless evidence to show the involvement of the vehicle is produced and insurance company did not adduced any evidence creating doubt on the involvement of the offending vehicle".

In the instant case on hand also the respondent No.1 and 2 have not led any evidence.
More over the respondent No.2 insurance company has not produced any evidence to show the incorrect involvement of the vehicle.
As such this ratio decidendi is also applicable to the case on hand.

14. Further it is relevant to relied on the decision reported in 2011 ACJ 926 in case of Kusum Lata and others V/s Satbir and others (AIR 2011 SC 1234) wherein it was held that the eyewitness in these types of case is prime importance.

15. Further more the respondent No.2 contended that offending lorry was traced after some days from the date of accident and it is an doubtful circumstances.
It is relevant to note that the FIR was lodged on the very same day of accident that too soon after the accident.
The mere non tracing of offending vehicle by the police is not at all fatal to the case of the petitioners herein.
The non tracing of the vehicle is just an little set-back to the investigation.

In this regard the petitioners have relied on the decision reported in 2022 ACJ 2003 in case of Janabai and others V/s ICICI Lombard General Ins.Co.Ltd., wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court held that there was dispute with regard to the involvement of the vehicle.

In the instant case on hand also the respondent No.1 being the owner of the vehicle has not filed any complaint for false implication.
As such the version of IO in the absence of any contra evidence has to be taken in to consideration.

In connected to the facts of the instant case, the petitioners has relied on the decision of Alahabad High Court reported in 2022 ACJ 2341 in case of Sarita Sharma and other V/s Mohd.
Usman and others, wherein it is held as under :
"Accident - Involvement of vehicle - Contention that FIR was lodged against an unknown truck and site plant also does not mention the registration number of offending truck therefore offending truck was implanted - FIR was lodged within 4  hours of the accident and there was non opportunity for claimants to plant a vehicle in such short time -

Whether offending truck was involved in the accident - Held :

17. Return back to the factual matrix in the instant case on hand also soon after the accident i.e.,
within the lapse of 7 hours the FIR was lodged and there was no room for the claimants to plant a vehicle in such a short term.
But in the instant case on hand the evidence of PW.2 being the Investigating officer lends helping hand to the petitioners in order to prove the involvement of the vehicle.
18. This Court does not find any toxic nexus between the claimants with that of insured with active collusion with the police authority.
The petitioners have clearly established the factum of involvement of the insured vehicle.
In order to prove the above said fact the petitioners have mainly relied on the Ex.P.4 and 5 documents.
On close perusal of the same it reflects that, there is an rash and negligence driving on the part of the offending vehicle.
No doubt the accident happened on the left side of the lane i.e., in the lane of egde of the road.
When such being the case their could not be any negligence attributed to the deceased for walking on the road which is meant for speeding vehicles in the said road.
As such this Court does not find any rashness or factum of volunteer not fit injuria on the part of deceased.

19. Further it is pertinent to note that the respondent No.2 has not made any effort to examine the driver of the offending vehicle before this Court and also not made any attempt to serve summon the hospital authorities to examine the MRO's to produce the MLC and police intimation.
From material placed on record it is clearly emanating that the accident happened because of shear negligence on the part of the Tipper lorry driver.
Even the charge sheet as per Ex.P.13 is also filed as against the Tipper lorry driver for the offences punishable u/s 279 & 304(A) of IPC.
As such there is no impediment holding that there is a negligence on the part of the driver of Tipper lorry.
Viewed from any angle this Court does not find any reason to distrust the version of the petitioners herein.
The discussion supra makes it is abundantly clear that the accident occurred solely due to the rash negligent driving of the Tipper lorry by its driver.
As such, this Tribunal answers issue No.2 In the Affirmative.

sentences.text: ISSUE NO.1 :
The petitioners claim that petitioner No.1 is the husband and petitioner No.2 to 5 are the children and petitioner No.6 is the mother in law of the deceased.
During the pendency of the case, the petitioner No.7 being the father in law of deceased died on 12.03.2025 and as per order of this Court he was deleted on 17.04.2025.
The ration card, Aadhar cards and Election ID cards marked at Ex's.P.14 to 28 and contents of the police papers do fortify the said fact.
It is pertinent to note that this relationship of the petitioners with the deceased has not been disputed by the respondents.
21. It is to be remembered as a principle of law that suggestions in cross-examination are no evidence.
Mere hurling of some suggestions which are denied can hardly take the place of proof or evidence.
The petitioners No.6 and 7 are the mother in law and father in law of the deceased.

Further it is to be noted herein that they are the depending upon the income of their son i.e.,
husband of deceased and not on the deceased Lakshmamma.
The petitioner No.7 died during the pendency of the petition and petitioner No.6 being the mother in law of the deceased is not dependent on the deceased.
Such suspicions cannot have any place in the realm of appreciation of evidence.
Be that as it may, on the basis of evidence placed on record, I hold that the petitioners are the legal representatives of the deceased Smt. Lakshmamma 22.
However the question that arises for consideration is that whether such status of legal representative alone will give rise to get an entitlement for compensation.
The answer would be in the negative.
Mere status of a legal representative alone is not sufficient to make a claim.
To put it differently, dependency is the criteria to award compensation.
In this view of the matter petitioners No.6 cannot be said to be dependent on the earnings of their daughter-in-law (deceased).
Under such circumstances only the petitioners No.1 to 5 are entitled for compensation under the head 'Loss of dependency'.
Hence, I answer to issue No.1 Partly in the Affirmative.
23. ISSUE NO.3 :
In this case the petitioners have claimed the compensation on the death of deceased in the road traffic accident.
The petitioners contended that deceased was working as agriculturist and earning a sum of Rs.35,000/- p.m.
In order to substantiate the above said fact absolutely no string of evidence is produced before this Court.
It is relevant to rely on a decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka rendered on Division Bench in the case of Ananda v/s Arjun and another in MFA.No.101144/2020 (MV) dated.05.07.2023.

entities.text: Ananda v/s Arjun and another in MFA.No.101144/2020 (MV)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has laid down the following principles in para No.8(b) are as here under :
"(b) The accident is of the year 2017.
The Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.7,000/- per month as against the claim of Rs.2,50,000/- per annum.
To substantiate the said claim, the injured claimant has not placed any material on record, it is for the Courts and Tribunals to assess the income notionally.
The notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for the accident of the year 2017 is Rs.10,250/-.

In the absence of any material produced by the claimant to prove his income, it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/-
per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant"

sentences.text: 8 As such this court is taking the notional income as prescribed by the Karnataka Legal Service Authority, Bengaluru.
Therefore in view of the above decision, the accident was occurred in the year 2023.
Therefore, Rs.16,000/- has to be taken into consideration as monthly income of the deceased.

24. The petitioners have produced the Aadhar card to show the age of the deceased as per Ex.P27,
wherein the date of birther of the deceased is mentioned as 01.01.1987, which indicates that she was aged (36 years 11 months 8 days) 37 years on the date of accident.

Therefore the appropriate multiplier as per Sarla Verma's case for the said age group is '15'.
25.

As per the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others), if the person died in the motor accident, the income with respect to the future prospect has to taken into consideration while awarding compensation.

entities.text: 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Apex Court has provide the chart for age of the deceased and percentage for future prospects in between below the age of 40 years 40%, 40 years to 50 years 25% and 50 to 60 years 10%.
The deceased is not a permanent Employee and not a fixed salary person and she died at the age of 37 years.
Therefore, in this case, 40% income has to be taken into consideration for future prospects.

Further as stated above that, as on the date of accident, deceased aged about 37 years and as such, 40% is added to the income of the deceased, then it comes to Rs.22,400/- p.m.
(Rs.16,000/- + 6,400/- i.e. 40%).
26. The deceased died living behind 5 dependents.

As per principle laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarala Verma Case, 1/4th of her income is required to be deducted towards her personal expenses which comes to Rs.16,800/- p.m. (Rs.22,400 - Rs.5,600 = Rs.16,800/-).
27. The income of the deceased is taken as Rs.16,800/- p.m. and the multiplier '15' is applied, then the loss of dependency comes to Rs.30,24,000/- (Rs.16,800 X 12 X 15).

Considering the above facts,
this Tribunal deems it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.30,24,000/- under the head of loss of dependency.

28. Further, as Law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others, the compensation towards loss to estate, funeral expenses and consortium is to be awarded.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioners contended that they have spent substantial amount towards transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies etc., but no documents are produced.

Hence this Tribunal award Rs.18,150/- towards loss to estate and Rs.18,150/- towards funeral expenses as enhanced at the rate of 10% on every 3 years and Rs.48,400/- towards consortium to the petitioner No.1.
By applying the observations made in the aforesaid case, as more than 6 years elapsed from the date of order amount of consortium, funeral expense and loss of estate to be enhanced.

29. In this case, the petitioner No.2 to 5 are the children of the deceased and as per the decision reported in (2018) 12 SCC 130 in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others, the petitioner No.2 to 5 are entitled for filial consortium, as the filial consortium is the right of the parents and children to get compensation in the case of an Manjunatha Also Called As C.N. ... vs Narayanaswamy N on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82891407/

31. REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% per annum is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
32. There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the owner of the Tipper lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-43-A-1551 and respondent No.2 being the insurer thereof are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioners together with interest @ 6% p.a from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.

Hence issue No.3 is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.

opennyai_summary.facts: This claim petition is filed under Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the death caused in a Road Traffic accident.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the driver of the insured vehicle did not possess valid & effective DL and further the said insured vehicle did not holding valid and effective Permit and FC.
5. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners proves that they are the legal heirs and dependents of the deceased ?
2) Whether the petitioners prove that the deceased succumbed to the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident that occurred on 09.12.2023 at about 6.28 to 6.40 p.m., near Narayanappa Land on Balepura - Channarayapattana, Channarayapattana Manjunatha Also Called As C.N. ... vs Narayanaswamy N on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82891407/
3
Hobli, Bengaluru District, due to actionable negligence of the driver of Tipper Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-43-A-1551 ?
3) Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation as prayed? If so, at what rate and from whom ?
4) What order or award ?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
When such is the case while analyzing the case filed under benevolent legislation this Court cannot expect strict proof of the same.
No strict proof of evidence can be expected in claim petition of like nature.
From his evidence it could be culled out there is absolutely no toxic nexus between the respondent No.1 who being the owner of the offending vehicle and the petitioners.
In the instant case on hand also the respondent No.1 and 2 have not led any evidence.
More over the respondent No.2 insurance company has not produced any evidence to show the incorrect involvement of the vehicle.
As such this ratio decidendi is also applicable to the case on hand.
Further relied on the decision reported in 2018 (2) AKR 407 in case of Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd, Hubli V/s Smt. Indrawwa Gurupadappa Nesur and others wherein also in the above said cited decision the eye witness to the accident had not stated with regard to the registration number.
In the instant case on hand also, the eye witnesses have not given the registration number of the vehicle.
It is relevant to note that the FIR was lodged on the very same day of accident that too soon after the accident.
The mere non tracing of offending vehicle by the police is not at all fatal to the case of the petitioners herein.
The non tracing of the vehicle is just an little set-back to the investigation.
17. Return back to the factual matrix in the instant case on hand also soon after the accident i.e.,
within the lapse of 7 hours the FIR was lodged and there was no room for the claimants to plant a vehicle in such a short term.
But in the instant case on hand the evidence of PW.2 being the Investigating officer lends helping hand to the petitioners in order to prove the involvement of the vehicle.
18. This Court does not find any toxic nexus between the claimants with that of insured with active collusion with the police authority.
The petitioners have clearly established the factum of involvement of the insured vehicle.
In order to prove the above said fact the petitioners have mainly relied on the Ex.P.4 and 5 documents.
On close perusal of the same it reflects that, there is an rash and negligence driving on the part of the offending vehicle.
When such being the case their could not be any negligence attributed to the deceased for walking on the road which is meant for speeding vehicles in the said road.
As such this Court does not find any rashness or factum of volunteer not fit injuria on the part of deceased.
From material placed on record it is clearly emanating that the accident happened because of shear negligence on the part of the Tipper lorry driver.
Even the charge sheet as per Ex.P.13 is also filed as against the Tipper lorry driver for the offences punishable u/s 279 & 304(A) of IPC.
As such there is no impediment holding that there is a negligence on the part of the driver of Tipper lorry.
21. It is to be remembered as a principle of law that suggestions in cross-examination are no evidence.
Mere hurling of some suggestions which are denied can hardly take the place of proof or evidence.
The petitioners No.6 and 7 are the mother in law and father in law of the deceased.
The petitioner No.7 died during the pendency of the petition and petitioner No.6 being the mother in law of the deceased is not dependent on the deceased.
Mere status of a legal representative alone is not sufficient to make a claim.
To put it differently, dependency is the criteria to award compensation.
In this view of the matter petitioners No.6 cannot be said to be dependent on the earnings of their daughter-in-law (deceased).
Under such circumstances only the petitioners No.1 to 5 are entitled for compensation under the head 'Loss of dependency'.
The deceased is not a permanent Employee and not a fixed salary person and she died at the age of 37 years.
Therefore, in this case, 40% income has to be taken into consideration for future prospects.

27. The income of the deceased is taken as Rs.16,800/- p.m. and the multiplier '15' is applied, then the loss of dependency comes to Rs.30,24,000/- (Rs.16,800 X 12 X 15).
Considering the above facts,
this Tribunal deems it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.30,24,000/- under the head of loss of dependency.
Hence this Tribunal award Rs.18,150/- towards loss to estate and Rs.18,150/- towards funeral expenses as enhanced at the rate of 10% on every 3 years and Rs.48,400/- towards consortium to the petitioner No.1.
